items.title: US unemployment rate
items.why: The share of people in the US labour force who are out of work and looking for a job, from the monthly household survey of the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is one of the most watched summaries of the job market.
items.lag: usually published in the first week of the following month

source.name: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED

items.reading: 4.2% now, down 0.1 percentage points over 6 months. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 4.1% to 4.5% and sits in the middle of that range.

next.question: Will the US unemployment rate for October 2026 be higher than 4.2%?

items.title: US weekly jobless claims
items.why: The number of people who filed a first claim for unemployment benefits in a week. It is published every Thursday and moves quickly, so it is an early sign of layoffs.
items.lag: published on the Thursday after the week ends

source.name: US Department of Labor, via FRED

items.reading: 194,000 now, down 13,000 over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 189,000 to 235,000 and sits near the bottom of that range.

next.question: Will US initial jobless claims for the week ending 7 November 2026 be above 197,000, the average of the last 4 weeks?

items.title: US monthly job gains
items.why: The change in the number of non-farm jobs in the US from one month to the next, the “jobs added” figure in the headlines. Early figures are revised later, and this question uses the first value that appears.
items.lag: usually published on the first Friday of the following month

source.name: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED

items.reading: 29 thousand jobs now, down 185 thousand jobs over 6 months. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from -156 to 214 and sits in the middle of that range.

next.question: Will US employers add more than 65 thousand jobs in October 2026, the average of the last 6 months?

items.title: Indeed software development job postings
items.why: Postings for software development jobs on Indeed in the US, relative to 1 February 2020 (set to 100). A measure of how much employers are hiring in the field.
items.lag: updated daily with a short delay
items.reading: 80.8 now, up 6.2 over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 65.9 to 80.8 and sits near the top of that range.

next.question: Will the Indeed software development job postings be higher on 30 October 2026 than on 23 October 2026 (80.8)?

items.title: Denmark unemployment rate (registered)
items.why: Registered unemployed people as a share of the Danish labour force (gross unemployment), the figure Danish media and the government quote. It was about 3% in 2026. It is lower than the survey-based rate below because it counts only people registered as unemployed.
items.lag: published about a month after the month ends
items.reading: 3.1% now, up 0.1 percentage points over 6 months. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 2.9% to 3.1% and sits near the top of that range.

next.question: Will the Denmark unemployment rate (registered) for October 2026 be higher than 3.1%?

items.title: Denmark unemployment rate (labour-force survey)
items.why: The international (ILO) definition: people without work who are looking for it and available to start, measured from a survey and harmonised across countries by Eurostat. It is roughly twice the registered rate because it counts people who are not registered, such as many students, and it jumps around from month to month because it comes from a sample.
items.lag: published about six weeks after the month ends
items.reading: 6.8% now, up 0.2 percentage points over 6 months. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 5.8% to 7.2% and sits in the middle of that range.

next.question: Will the Denmark unemployment rate (labour-force survey, Eurostat) for October 2026 be higher than 6.8%?

items.title: US inflation (year on year)
items.why: The change in US consumer prices compared with the same month a year earlier, the standard measure of inflation.
items.lag: usually published in the middle of the following month

source.name: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED

items.reading: 3.7% now, up 0.4 percentage points over 6 months. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 2.4% to 4.2% and sits in the middle of that range.

next.question: Will the US inflation (year on year) for October 2026 be higher than 3.7%?

items.title: US effective federal funds rate
items.why: The interest rate banks charge each other overnight, the rate the Federal Reserve steers. It sets the base for borrowing costs across the economy. It moves in steps at policy meetings, so most months it hardly changes.
items.lag: the monthly average is published at the start of the following month

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve, via FRED

items.reading: 3.88% now, up 0.24 percentage points over 6 months. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 3.63% to 3.88% and sits near the top of that range.

next.question: Will the US effective federal funds rate for November 2026 be lower than 3.88%?

items.title: US 10-year Treasury yield
items.why: The yield on 10-year US government bonds, a benchmark for mortgage and company borrowing rates. Short-term moves are close to a coin flip, so these questions mostly teach how little can be predicted.

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve, via FRED

items.reading: 4.91% now, up 0.13 percentage points over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 4.03% to 5.31% and sits in the middle of that range.

next.question: Will the US 10-year Treasury yield close higher on 9 November 2026 than on 2 November 2026 (4.91%)?

items.title: S&P 500 stock index
items.why: An index of 500 large US companies, the usual shorthand for the stock market. These questions teach base rates: the index rises in more weeks than it falls, yet any single week is close to a coin flip.

source.name: S&P Dow Jones Indices, via FRED

items.reading: 7,541.4 points now, down 177.2 points over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 6,343.72 to 7,807.24 and sits near the top of that range.

next.question: Will the S&P 500 stock index close higher on 4 November 2026 than on 28 October 2026 (7,743.98)?

items.title: US 30-year mortgage rate
items.why: The average rate on a 30-year fixed US home loan, from Freddie Mac's weekly survey. It follows long-term bond yields and shows what borrowing to buy a home costs.
items.reading: 7.24% now, up 0.53 percentage points over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 5.98% to 7.4% and sits near the top of that range.

next.question: Will the US 30-year mortgage rate for November 2026 be higher than 7.24%?

items.title: US dollar in Danish kroner
items.why: How many Danish kroner one US dollar buys. The krone is tied to the euro, so this moves with the euro–dollar rate. It matters for anyone paid in dollars and living in Denmark, or the other way round.
items.lag: daily, noon buying rate in New York

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve, via FRED

items.reading: 6.695 DKK per USD now, up 0.262 DKK per USD over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 6.283 to 6.695 and sits near the top of that range.

next.question: Will the US dollar in Danish kroner close higher on 6 November 2026 than on 23 October 2026 (6.673)?

items.title: WTI crude oil price
items.why: The spot price of West Texas Intermediate crude oil, a benchmark for energy costs that feed into inflation and transport prices. Day-to-day moves are close to a coin flip.

source.name: US Energy Information Administration, via FRED

items.reading: 103.37 USD per barrel now, up 11.89 USD per barrel over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 55.44 to 114.58 and sits near the top of that range.

next.question: Will the WTI crude oil price close higher on 3 November 2026 than on 27 October 2026 (103.37)?

items.title: VIX volatility index
items.why: The market's expected swing in US stocks over the next 30 days, drawn from option prices and often called the fear gauge. Low readings mean calm, spikes mean investors are paying for protection.

source.name: Chicago Board Options Exchange, via FRED

items.reading: 21.15 points now, up 5.85 points over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 14.08 to 30.61 and sits in the middle of that range.

next.question: Will the VIX volatility index close higher on 5 November 2026 than on 29 October 2026 (17.2)?

items.title: arXiv papers on underwater acoustics and sonar
items.why: Papers submitted to arXiv in a week whose abstracts mention underwater acoustics, sonar or hydrophones. It shows how much researchers are publishing on the topic, not how good the work is.
items.reading: 3 papers now, down 4 papers over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 0 to 9 and sits in the middle of that range.

next.question: Will arXiv receive more than 6 papers on underwater acoustics and sonar in the week starting 9 November 2026, the average of the last 8 weeks?

items.title: arXiv papers on language models
items.why: Papers submitted to arXiv in a week whose abstracts mention language models. A measure of research activity in the area that dominates AI news, not of quality.
items.reading: 732 papers now, down 150 papers over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 414 to 1,556 and sits in the middle of that range.

next.question: Will arXiv receive more than 950 papers on language models in the week starting 9 November 2026, the average of the last 8 weeks?

items.title: arXiv papers on world models
items.why: Papers submitted to arXiv in a week whose abstracts mention world models, models that learn how an environment changes in response to actions. A gauge of how fast the idea is spreading in research.
items.reading: 64 papers now, up 13 papers over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 13 to 164 and sits in the middle of that range.

next.question: Will arXiv receive more than 96 papers on world models in the week starting 9 November 2026, the average of the last 8 weeks?

items.title: arXiv papers on sound source localization
items.why: Papers submitted to arXiv in a week about locating sound sources or estimating direction of arrival, the field behind robot hearing and passive sonar.
items.reading: 3 papers now, up 3 papers over 8 weeks. Over the last 12 months it has ranged from 0 to 7 and sits in the middle of that range.

next.question: Will arXiv receive more than 4 papers on sound source localization in the week starting 2 November 2026, the average of the last 8 weeks?
